title: Samosa

seo.title: How to Make Samosa — Easy Pakistani Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Samosa. This easy Pakistani recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Samosa — a beloved Pakistani classic

description: Samosas are a beloved Pakistani appetizer, featuring a crispy pastry shell filled with a savory mixture of spiced potatoes and peas, sometimes with minced meat. These triangular delights are deep-fried to golden perfection, offering a delightful crunch and burst of flavor with every bite. They are perfect for tea time, parties, or as a delicious snack.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, and carom seeds. Add melted ghee or oil and mix until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Gradually add water and knead into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and let it rest for 15-20 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Filling
instructions.text: Heat a tablespoon of oil in a pan. Add chopped onions and saute until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute. Stir in all the dry spices: cumin, coriander, red chili, turmeric, garam masala, and amchur. Cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine Filling Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the boiled and mashed potatoes and green peas to the pan. Mix well with the spices, ensuring everything is evenly coated. Cook for another 5 minutes, mashing lightly to combine flavors. Stir in fresh coriander leaves. Let the filling cool completely.

instructions.title: Shape the Samosas
instructions.text: Divide the dough into equal small balls. Roll each ball into an oval shape, about 6-7 inches long. Cut the oval in half lengthwise to create two semi-circles. Apply a little water along the straight edge of one semi-circle.

instructions.title: Fill and Seal Samosas
instructions.text: Bring the straight edges together to form a cone shape, pressing firmly to seal. Spoon a generous amount of the cooled potato filling into the cone. Apply water to the remaining open edges and pinch them together, creating pleats on one side for the classic samosa shape. Ensure a tight seal to prevent the filling from coming out during frying.

instructions.title: Fry the Samosas
instructions.text: Heat oil for deep frying in a heavy-bottomed pan or wok over medium-low heat. The oil should not be too hot, or the samosas will brown too quickly without cooking through. Gently place a few samosas into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry until golden brown and crispy on all sides, turning occasionally. This will take about 8-10 minutes per batch.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Once fried, remove the samosas with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels. Serve hot with mint chutney, tamarind chutney, or ketchup.

tips: For a truly crispy crust, ensure your dough is firm and rested. When frying, start with medium-low heat and gradually increase it, allowing the dough to cook through evenly.
The filling must be completely cooled before shaping the samosas. Warm filling can make the dough soggy and difficult to handle, leading to a less crispy exterior.
Samosas can be prepared and frozen before frying. Arrange them on a baking sheet until solid, then transfer to a freezer-safe bag. Fry from frozen, adding a few extra minutes to the cooking time.
